title: Correctness advances by one step
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-tape Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let $x$ be a finite Boolean input, let $A$ be a Boolean answer table, and let $x_b$ be a Boolean sequence. Suppose every local check passes under the numerical valuation determined by $M,A,W,x,x_b$ for all times and work indices below $2^W$, all input indices at most $|x|+1$, and every check type. If the table correctly describes the machine at time $t$, in the sense that it gives every state-and-output answer, every work-tape symbol at offsets satisfying $|d|+t\le 2^W-1$, and every input symbol at offsets satisfying $|d|\le |x|+1$, and if $t+1<2^W$, then the table correctly describes the machine at time $t+1$ in the same sense.
